messages:
ashley: Heads-up — around 09:12 UTC Route53 flipped most traffic for customer-facing endpoints from eu-west-1 -> us-west-2 via latency-based failover. That region had just been holding burst capacity for Dedicated and we ended up saturating GPU pools. Seeing model pods OOM/killed and backend 5xxs.

matt: omg, did health checks fail in eu-west or was R53 logic mis-triggered?

ashley: Health checks for the geo-policy returned unhealthy for eu-west. Digging in — it looks like our eu-west NAT egress config was recently tightened (egress SG + NAT GW rotation). Route53 health checks originate from outside our VPC and hit the public LB IP. I think the health check probes were blocked by a misapplied NACL on the public LB subnet.

jen: Can you paste the Route53 healthcheck logs or the LB access logs?

ashley: Pasted a snippet from the LB access log: 
```
https 2025-11-05T09:11:58.123Z app/my-public-lb 10.0.4.23:443 - 54.239.28.85:443 0.000 0.001 0.003 200 200 0 123 "GET /health HTTP/1.1" "Route53HealthCheck/1.0" - - arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:123456789012:targetgroup/tg/abcdef
```
And later: \n```
... request from 54.239.28.85 timed out \n```
Looks like some probes succeeded and some timed out — intermittent network path.

paul: Intermittent probes + low TTL on latency policy could cause R53 to rapidly shift traffic. What's our GeoDNS TTL?

ashley: Currently TTL=60s with latency-based routing and health checks. Because probes flapped for ~2 minutes we got a mass failover.

matt: And us-west2 couldn't handle the sudden spike because Dedicated GPU pool scaling is not instantaneous for that class of Instance/quantized models. We hit queue backpressure and request timeouts.

jen: Two problems then: (1) health checks flapping due to egress/NAT or NACL, (2) routing policy too aggressive for stateful GPU-backed endpoints. Suggest the following: set TTL=10s? wait, that makes it more aggressive. Maybe increase TTL and switch to weighted fallback with gradual shift. Also add a sticky policy for in-flight model sessions.

paul: Agreed — increase TTL to 300s for these endpoints and change latency-based -> failover with controlled weights. Also add a guard: only failover after N consecutive healthcheck failures across multiple vantage points. Route53 supports 'health check count' via external checks? We can implement in our control plane: track health and flip weights via API after 3m sustained failure.

ashley: +1 on guard. For immediate mitigation I re-opened NACL rule to allow AWS health-check IP ranges to the LB port (ingress 54.239.0.0/16 etc) until infra finishes permanent fix.

infra-bot: ACTION LOGGED: NACL rule change (rollback) applied by ashley at 09:20 UTC. Ticket INF-4812 created for permanent fix.

matt: For capacity: I'm going to bump Dedicated us-west2 GPU pool by 30% for the next 6 hours to absorb requests while we stabilize routing. Will monitor cost impact.

jen: Can we instead route only a small % to us-west2 until warmup completes? If we do hard failover the spike hits instantly. Need gradual ramp (A/B weights).

ashley: Yes — I'm going to update the control-plane rollout policy to do a canary weight shift: 10% -> 30% -> 60% over 10 minutes. Also adding a circuit-breaker so if latency > 300ms we revert.

paul: Also important: health checks currently point at /health which does a lightweight HTTP 200. But it doesn't validate internal cache warming or model readiness. We should use an enhanced health endpoint that checks model warm state OR use separate readiness probes for Route53.

matt: Good call. If the health endpoint is too permissive we get false positives that mask backend symptoms. Add model-ready check that looks at KV cache population or at least model process memory usage.

jen: Follow-ups: 
- ashley: add temporary NACL allowance + open INF-4812 with details (done)
- ashley: change routing to weighted canary and add circuit-breaker policy (in progress)
- matt: scale us-west2 Dedicated pool + monitor cost (in progress)
- paul: propose TTL/strategy change to product/networking and draft terraform change for Route53 (blocked until canary tests)
- jen: implement enhanced readiness endpoint and add to LB target group health check path

sre-oncall: Adding an automated alert: if > 20% of requests shift region in < 2m AND any region's GPU utilization > 80% -> create high-priority page and runbook.

deploy-bot: Rollout triggered by ashley: route-control v2 -> canary weight update queued.

ashley: TL;DR: Route53 health checks were intermittently blocked because of recent egress/NAT changes. That triggered a fast latency-failover and we experienced a capacity spike in the fallback region, exposing that our failover policy and health semantics are too aggressive for GPU-backed endpoints. Short-term fixes applied (NACL rollback, scale-up, canary weights). Long-term: change routing to weighted failover + higher TTL + stronger health/readiness semantics.

matt: Also let's capture cost impact: I'll post a short report for finance on the additional Dedicated spend and the delta caused by failover.

paul: I'll prepare the terraform PR for weighted routing + health guard. Will ping for review once draft is ready.

jen: I'll start on readiness endpoint and add an integration test to ensure Route53 probes always hit a synthetic warm endpoint.

ashley: Thanks team. Will keep thread updated with metrics (latency, region weights, GPU pool utilization).
